manuscript: Structural testability does not imply predictable contraction in finite ecological world sets
primary_claim: Structural adequacy of a finite declared world universe can be audited without biological responses, but later evidence-driven world survival is not generally identifiable from global response-blind graph structure alone because compatibility depends on positive-node placement.

supported.claim: The prospectively frozen NEON structure-only regime rule failed.
supported.evidence: 2/9 exact regime matches; seven saturated and two contracting scored sites; one-sided upper-tail p versus fixed one-third reference = 0.8569323781943813.

supported.claim: The frozen rule systematically underpredicted world survival among scored NEON sites.
supported.evidence: All nine scored sites had observed surviving-world fractions above their frozen forecasts; mean observed fraction 0.9351851851851851 versus mean forecast 0.5185185185185185.

supported.claim: Finite-world updating is not intrinsically restricted to endpoint outcomes.
supported.evidence: DELA retained 3/4 distinct worlds and DSNY retained 2/3.

supported.claim: For exactly two positives on any nonempty, noncomplete undirected world graph, both survival and failure are possible with the same graph and positive-set size.
supported.evidence: Adjacent-pair versus non-adjacent-pair witness theorem; synthetic tests in test_world_survival_identifiability.py.

supported.claim: Structural adequacy and later contraction are distinct inferential objects.
supported.evidence: Adequacy is computed before response access from graph properties; survival is evaluated after positive-node placement is revealed.

prohibited: The 0.5 cutoff should be retuned on the consumed NEON outcome.
The seven registry-mismatch sites can be repaired and scored inside the same programme.
All finite-world systems are inherently saturated.
A graph-only structural summary universally predicts later survival regime.
The NEON guild result is a taxon-level validation.
A surviving world is the true historical dispersal process.
This programme alters the closed EOG-WF Layer-B predictive conclusion.

interpretation_boundary.adequacy: Response-blind structural certificate about whether the declared finite world family is testable at declared scales.
interpretation_boundary.survival: Response-conditioned compatibility state after positive observations are located on the graph.
interpretation_boundary.prediction: Requires additional assumptions about positive-node placement if attempted probabilistically.
